# ui::ClipScope

Header: `winui/render/Renderer.hpp`.

Pushes a clip when it is made and pops it when it goes out of scope, so an early return cannot leave the clip pushed.

Example: 
```cpp
class Caption : public ui::Element
{
    std::string label_ = "A caption longer than its box";

    void render_override(ui::Renderer& r, const ui::RenderContext& context) const override
    {
        const ui::Theme&    theme = context.theme;
        const ui::ClipScope clip{r, bounds()};
        r.draw_text(label_, bounds(), theme.colors().text, theme.type.body); // clipped to bounds()
    }
};
```

## ClipScope

```cpp
ClipScope(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds)
```

Clips to `bounds` ([Renderer::push_clip()](renderer.md#push_clip)).

## ClipScope

```cpp
ClipScope(Renderer& renderer, Point center, float radius_x, float radius_y)
```

Clips to an ellipse ([Renderer::push_clip_ellipse()](renderer.md#push_clip_ellipse)).

## ClipScope

```cpp
ClipScope(Renderer& renderer, const Rect& bounds, float radius)
```

Clips to a rect with rounded corners ([Renderer::push_clip_rounded_rect()](renderer.md#push_clip_rounded_rect)).

## ~ClipScope

```cpp
~ClipScope()
```

Pops the clip.
